source: NCERT Our Wondrous World (Class V), Chapter 2

overview.bigIdea: The river Godavari tells its own story: **where it begins, how it grows, how it helps people, and what hurts it**. Rivers are a shared gift – we must keep them clean and use water wisely.

lessons.title: The Godavari’s journey
lessons.hook: “I have no feet, but I travel far…” **Who am I?** A river! Meet the Godavari, who starts as a little stream and grows into India’s second longest river.

core.def: Trimbakeshwar, Brahmagiri Hills of the Western Ghats, Maharashtra.
1,465 km; joins the Bay of Bengal. Second longest river in India after the Ganga.
Small streams that join a river and make it bigger – e.g. Indravati, Manjira, Sabari.
Perennial rivers flow all year (Godavari); seasonal rivers flow only in the rainy season.
Where the river spreads into many small streams before meeting the sea – Coringa mangrove forests.

explain: States on its way include Maharashtra, Telangana, Chhattisgarh, Odisha and Andhra Pradesh (see the map).
It passes rich forests with tigers, barking deer, the Indian golden gecko and red sandalwood trees.
It is called Dakshina Ganga; the Godavari Pushkaram is celebrated near Nashik.

example.q: Describe the journey of the Godavari. (3 marks)
steps: It begins at Trimbakeshwar in the Western Ghats in Maharashtra as a small stream.
Tributaries and rainwater join it, making it wider and stronger as it flows 1,465 km.
It forms a delta and joins the Bay of Bengal at the Coringa mangrove forests.
example.answer: Start → grows with tributaries → delta → Bay of Bengal.

mistakes: Saying it joins the Arabian Sea.
Mixing up tributary (joins the river) and delta (river splits at the sea).
lessons.tip: Learn the journey as a 4-word chain: Trimbakeshwar → tributaries → delta → Bay of Bengal.
lessons.memory: Start small, grow tall, split at the sea!

lessons.title: How rivers support lives · Dams
lessons.hook: Open a tap and water flows. **But where did it start?** Often in a river far away, carried by pipes and canals, and stored behind giant dams.

core.def: Water for drinking, cooking, washing, growing food and factories; livelihoods like fishing and boating.
A giant wall that blocks a river and stores water in a reservoir.
Water in dry seasons for drinking and crops; making electricity.
Flood land that was home to animals and people; many must leave their homes.

explain: More than 900 dams store the Godavari’s water.
Ecotourism: visiting nature to enjoy and learn without harming it.

example.q: Write one benefit and one problem of building a dam. (2 marks)
steps: Benefit: it stores water for drinking, crops and electricity even in dry seasons.
Problem: it floods land, so people and animals lose their homes.

mistakes: Writing only benefits when asked for problems too.
lessons.tip: Use ‘but’ to show both sides: ‘A dam stores water, but it floods homes.’
lessons.memory: Dam = store water, but some lose their homes.

lessons.title: What pollutes a river
lessons.hook: Stir sugar into one glass of water and oil into another. **One looks clear, one does not.** But clear water is not always safe!

core.def: Waste, plastic and dirty water from homes and factories make river water unsafe.
Sugar and salt dissolve (disappear) in water; oil and sand do not.
Fertilisers washed from fields make plants grow very fast and cover the river, choking fish.
Use eco-friendly products, create less waste, Namami Gange programme.

explain: Fish, turtles and birds have nowhere else to go when their river is polluted.
Harmful chemicals or soapy water can hide in water that looks clean.

example.q: How do fertilisers harm a river? (2 marks)
steps: Fertilisers from fields wash into the river and make plants grow very fast.
They cover the river like a green blanket, so fish find it hard to breathe and the water becomes unsafe.
example.answer: Fast plant growth → green blanket → fish choke.

mistakes: Thinking clear water is always clean.
lessons.tip: Always end with a solution: ‘We can use less waste and eco-friendly products.’

lessons.title: Floods, droughts and saving water
lessons.hook: Sometimes the river roars and floods the land. Sometimes it runs dry. **Both too much and too little water cause trouble.**

core.def: Too much rain makes a river overflow its banks and flood houses, fields and roads.
Trees slow rainwater and help soil soak it up; without trees water runs off faster.
Get to higher ground, do not walk in flood water, do not touch power lines, keep an emergency bag.
When no water is available for a long time, families may have to move.
Turn off taps, fix leaks, reuse clean water for plants, remind others. Every drop counts!

explain: Chennai (2019) brought water by train because reservoirs dried up; Bengaluru (2022) was flooded by heavy rain.
Water ATMs and the National Water Mission help people use water wisely.

example.q: List three flood safety tips. (3 marks)
steps: Do not walk or swim in flood water.
Do not touch power lines; keep an emergency bag with food, medicines and a flashlight.
example.answer: Higher ground · avoid flood water · stay away from power lines.

mistakes: Forgetting animals – free cattle and lead them to safety.
lessons.tip: Group flood tips into before, during and after.
lessons.memory: Up high, stay dry, power lines goodbye!

revision: The Godavari begins at **Trimbakeshwar** and flows **1,465 km** to the **Bay of Bengal**.
**Tributaries** join a river; a **delta** forms at the sea.
The Godavari is **perennial**; seasonal rivers flow only in the rains.
**Dams** store water in reservoirs but can flood homes.
Waste, soap and **fertilisers** pollute rivers; clear water may not be safe.
Trees reduce **floods**; save water – **every drop counts**.

sections.title: Map and story tips
items: Trace the Godavari on the map from west to east.
Mark its start, one tributary, one dam and the delta.
Tell the journey in 4 steps with ‘first, then, next, finally’.

sections.title: Writing answers that score
items: Read the question twice and underline the key word (why, how, name, list).
Answer in full sentences using words from the book – e.g. ‘Microbes need moisture, air and the right temperature to grow.’
For ‘why’ questions, give the reason with ‘because’.
For 2–3 mark answers, write 2–3 separate points.
Add one example from the chapter (Godavari, Disha’s pickle, the green school) to show you understand.
Draw and label a simple diagram when it helps – the water cycle, types of teeth, the river’s journey.

sections.title: The day before the test
items: Read the key facts sheet aloud once.
Do the Play & learn activities again – if you get every card right first time, you are ready.
Take one Check knowledge quiz at Hard level.

checklist: I can tell the Godavari’s journey in order.
I can explain tributary, delta and perennial river.
I can give one benefit and one problem of dams.
I can explain how rivers get polluted.
I can list flood safety tips and ways to save water.
exam.paperTitle: How this chapter is usually tested
exam.paperNote: Typical Class V school test pattern (1-mark MCQ, fill in the blanks, true/false and matching; 2–3 mark short answers; activity-based questions). Your school’s paper may differ slightly.

method: Built on how children learn best: start with a story or activity, sort and match ideas with your hands, say answers aloud before checking (active recall), and come back after 1, 3 and 7 days (spaced revision).
